# BitBadges

> BitBadges is a Cosmos SDK L1 with a native token standard (x/tokenization): collections, time-based balances, three-level transfer approvals with on-chain criteria, manager permissions, IBC wrapping, and EVM precompiles. Off-chain: a REST API, a TypeScript SDK, a CLI (`bb`), claims with plugins, Sign In with BitBadges, and MCP builder tools for AI agents.

Full corpus as one file: https://docs.bitbadges.io/llms-full.txt (also served as https://docs.bitbadges.io/for-llms.txt). Every page is also served as Markdown at its URL plus .md, for example https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/setup.md. OpenAPI: https://docs.bitbadges.io/openapi.json. API reference: https://docs.bitbadges.io/api-reference.

URL patterns: /token-standard/messages/msg-<kebab>, /token-standard/queries/<kebab>, /token-standard/approval-criteria/<kebab>, /cli/<group>, /api/..., /agents/skills/<skill-id>.

## Docs

- [Overview](https://docs.bitbadges.io/)
- [Quickstart](https://docs.bitbadges.io/start/quickstart): Install BitBadges, run a first query, and broadcast a first transaction in the CLI, TypeScript, the no-code site, or an AI agent.
- [Your First Collection](https://docs.bitbadges.io/start/first-collection): Idea to on-chain in one sitting: build a subscription token with an AI agent or the CLI, check it, simulate it, and sign it in the browser, with real output.
- [Using the Frontend](https://docs.bitbadges.io/using-the-frontend): What the bitbadges.io site is for, and a map of the pages that walk through browsing, signing, and managing tokens there.
  - [Connect a Wallet](https://docs.bitbadges.io/using-the-frontend/connect-a-wallet): How to connect a wallet on bitbadges.io, what signing in adds on top of connecting, and how bb1 and 0x addresses relate.
  - [Browse and Search](https://docs.bitbadges.io/using-the-frontend/browse-and-search): Find collections, accounts, and tokens on bitbadges.io from the home page, the browse page, and the global search bar.
  - [Collection Page](https://docs.bitbadges.io/using-the-frontend/collection-page): Read one collection on bitbadges.io: the Tokens, Distribution, Details, Linked Items, and Actions tabs, and what the permission grid means.
  - [Create Tab and In-Site Forms](https://docs.bitbadges.io/using-the-frontend/create-tab-and-in-site-forms): The Create tab on bitbadges.io: the In-Site template forms, the Programmatic path for AI and CLI builds, and what each form step does.
  - [Review and Sign](https://docs.bitbadges.io/using-the-frontend/review-and-sign): The review-and-sign page at bitbadges.io/mint/local-builder: paste a transaction or a preview code, review it, and sign in your wallet.
  - [Developer Portal](https://docs.bitbadges.io/using-the-frontend/developer-portal): The Developer Portal at bitbadges.io/developer: API keys, claims, claim plugins, dynamic stores, OAuth apps, and what you created.
  - [Account and Balances](https://docs.bitbadges.io/using-the-frontend/account-and-balances): Your account page on bitbadges.io: the tokens you own, the ones you created or manage, your approvals, hidden tokens, and activity.
  - [Claims and Distribution](https://docs.bitbadges.io/using-the-frontend/claims-and-distribution): Claim a token from a claim link on bitbadges.io, read the criteria a claim checks, and find the claims you own in the Developer Portal.
- [Use Cases](https://docs.bitbadges.io/use-cases): One token standard, twelve products. Each page shows the approval fields that turn the standard into a stablecoin, a subscription, an agent vault, or a store.
  - [Stablecoins and Backed Tokens](https://docs.bitbadges.io/use-cases/stablecoins-and-backed-tokens): Issue a token backed 1:1 by USDC or any IBC coin. One invariant and two approvals give you deposit-to-mint, burn-to-withdraw, and an x/bank denom.
  - [Subscriptions](https://docs.bitbadges.io/use-cases/subscriptions): Sell access that renews on a schedule and expires on its own. One mint approval with a duration and a coin payment replaces the billing service.
  - [Payment Requests and Invoices](https://docs.bitbadges.io/use-cases/payment-requests-and-invoices): Let an agent or a merchant ask one payer for a fixed amount. The payer approves and pays in one signature, with no escrow and a built-in expiry.
  - [Bounties and Escrow](https://docs.bitbadges.io/use-cases/bounties-and-escrow): Lock funds at creation and release them on a verifier's vote, a denial, or a deadline. Three approvals, one escrow address, no contract.
  - [Agent Vaults and Spending Limits](https://docs.bitbadges.io/use-cases/agent-vaults-and-spending-limits): Give an AI agent funds with a daily cap, a time window, a recipient list, 2FA on withdrawals, and one-transaction revocation, all enforced by the chain.
  - [Token-Gated Access](https://docs.bitbadges.io/use-cases/token-gated-access): Gate an API route, a page, or a download behind token ownership with BB-402. A soulbound receipt and one JSON condition replace API keys.
  - [NFTs and Collectibles](https://docs.bitbadges.io/use-cases/nfts-and-collectibles): Mint 1-of-1s or editions, choose tradable, burnable, or soulbound per approval, and get listings and bids from user approvals instead of a contract.
  - [Crowdfunding and Auctions](https://docs.bitbadges.io/use-cases/crowdfunding-and-auctions): Raise toward a goal with claimable refunds, or sell one item to the best bid. Both are collections whose approvals read their own balances and a deadline.
  - [Prediction Markets](https://docs.bitbadges.io/use-cases/prediction-markets): Mint YES and NO pairs against USDC, trade them on a pool, and settle by a verifier's vote. Seven approvals and two alias denoms are the whole market.
  - [Loyalty Points and Credits](https://docs.bitbadges.io/use-cases/loyalty-points-and-credits): Sell prepaid credits at a fixed exchange rate, or pay a reward for every completed quest. Soulbound fungible tokens with a coin transfer on the mint approval.
  - [Memberships and Address Lists](https://docs.bitbadges.io/use-cases/memberships-and-address-lists): Keep an allowlist, a ban list, a DAO roster, or a five-minute 2FA token on-chain. Membership is a balance; the manager adds by minting and removes by burning.
  - [Product Catalogs and Commerce](https://docs.bitbadges.io/use-cases/product-catalogs-and-commerce): Sell SKUs on-chain with independent prices, supply caps, and burn-on-purchase. One purchase approval per product routes payment straight to the store.
- [Guides](https://docs.bitbadges.io/guides): Task guides for BitBadges. Start with the AI builder, then follow CLI, TypeScript SDK, and JSON examples for direct integration.
  - [Create a Collection](https://docs.bitbadges.io/guides/create-a-collection): Create an NFT or fungible token collection on BitBadges with the AI builder, the bb CLI, the TypeScript SDK, or raw MsgCreateCollection JSON.
  - [Mint and Distribute](https://docs.bitbadges.io/guides/mint-and-distribute): Mint BitBadges tokens to yourself or to the public, charge for mints, pay out from escrow, and control circulating supply.
  - [Set Transferability](https://docs.bitbadges.io/guides/set-transferability): Decide who can transfer, burn, trade, or force-move BitBadges tokens with collection approvals and user-level approvals.
  - [Lock Permissions](https://docs.bitbadges.io/guides/lock-permissions): Freeze supply, approvals, token IDs, metadata, or a whole BitBadges collection with collection permissions, and lock user permissions for escrow accounts.
  - [Distribute with Claims](https://docs.bitbadges.io/guides/distribute-with-claims): Configure a claim with plugins, simulate and complete it from your backend, verify success, and gate an on-chain mint with it.
  - [Build a Claim Plugin](https://docs.bitbadges.io/guides/build-a-claim-plugin): Write an HTTP endpoint that BitBadges calls during claims, register it in the developer portal, handle simulations and state safely, test it, and version it.
  - [Gate Access](https://docs.bitbadges.io/guides/gate-access): Gate an API or resource behind token ownership with BB-402. Server that returns 402, verifies a signed proof, and checks balances; client that answers it.
  - [Sign In Users](https://docs.bitbadges.io/guides/sign-in-users): Add Sign In with BitBadges to your app. Register an OAuth app, build the authorize URL, handle the callback, exchange the code, and check your own criteria.
  - [Wrap to an IBC Denom](https://docs.bitbadges.io/guides/wrap-to-an-ibc-denom): Add a cosmos coin wrapper path so BitBadges tokens convert 1:1 into an x/bank coin that moves over IBC, with the wrapper and unwrapper approvals it needs.
  - [Trade on the DEX](https://docs.bitbadges.io/guides/trade-on-the-dex): Find pools and prices, check balances, estimate and execute a swap, and add or remove liquidity on the BitBadges DEX from the CLI, TypeScript, or raw messages.
  - [Subscriptions and Time-Based Tokens](https://docs.bitbadges.io/guides/subscriptions-and-time-based-tokens): Sell recurring subscriptions, prepaid credit tokens, and expiring tokens on BitBadges with bb build subscription, bb build credit-token, and ownership times.
  - [Smart Tokens and Vaults](https://docs.bitbadges.io/guides/smart-tokens-and-vaults): Issue a BitBadges smart token backed 1:1 by an IBC coin, add withdraw limits and 2FA, and give an AI agent a USDC vault it can deposit to and withdraw from.
- [About](https://docs.bitbadges.io/about): Why BitBadges exists, the three theses behind it, the design decisions, and what the x/tokenization standard provides.
  - [Use Cases](https://docs.bitbadges.io/about/use-cases): What people build with the BitBadges token standard, grouped by domain, with the feature each use case relies on.
  - [Comparisons](https://docs.bitbadges.io/about/comparisons): How the BitBadges L1 and token standard compare to other chains and to ERC-3643, and how ERC-3643 works as an interface on BitBadges.
  - [BADGE Token](https://docs.bitbadges.io/about/badge-token): BADGE, the native coin of the BitBadges chain. Its purposes, supply and distribution, and the validator rewards and proof-of-authority model.
  - [Links and Brand](https://docs.bitbadges.io/about/links): Official BitBadges links: app, explorer, install, packages, API reference, socials, integrations, brand assets, and how to contribute.
  - [FAQ](https://docs.bitbadges.io/about/faq): Short answers on smart contracts, compliance enforcement, L1 versus L2, ERC compatibility, EVM extension, and the protocol fee schedule.

## Token Standard

- [Overview](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard): What the x/tokenization module is, how its pieces fit together, and the order to read this tab in.
- [Concepts](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/concepts): The mental model behind every BitBadges token on one page, plus the order to read the concept pages in.
  - [Accounts and Addresses](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/concepts/accounts): How Ethereum and Cosmos addresses map to one BitBadges account, and which form to show users.
  - [Uint Ranges](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/concepts/uint-ranges): The inclusive { start, end } range type that represents token IDs, times, and amounts everywhere in the module.
  - [Balances](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/concepts/balances): How a Balance combines an amount, token ID ranges, and ownership time ranges, and the rules for expanding, subtracting, and merging them.
  - [Collections](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/concepts/collections): Every field on a TokenCollection: metadata, inline customData metadata, standards, validTokenIds, defaultBalances, isArchived, and the pointer to invariants.
  - [Minting and Supply](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/concepts/minting-and-supply): The reserved Mint address, how circulating supply is defined, and how to cap or leave open the supply of a collection.
  - [Address Lists](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/concepts/address-lists): Reserved, inline, and stored address lists, the ! inversion syntax, and how Mint is handled in each.
  - [Transferability](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/concepts/transferability): The three approval levels (collection, outgoing, incoming), the fields of an approval, auto-approval flags, overrides, and how a transfer is validated.
  - [Prioritized Approvals](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/concepts/prioritized-approvals): Auto-scan vs prioritized approval matching, approval versions, the onlyCheckPrioritized flags, and the mustPrioritize criterion.
  - [Permissions](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/concepts/permissions): The manager role, the three permission states, first-match evaluation, and the action, token ID, and approval permission types for collections and users.
  - [Compliance Zones](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/concepts/compliance-zones): Why BitBadges enforces compliance at the boundary of x/tokenization instead of in every module, and how the open zone and compliance zone connect.
- [Approval Criteria](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/approval-criteria): The full approvalCriteria interface, which fields exist on which approval level, one line per criterion with a link, and the require* address flags.
  - [Address Checks](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/approval-criteria/address-checks): senderChecks, recipientChecks, and initiatorChecks: require or forbid EVM contracts and liquidity pools for each party of a transfer.
  - [Alt Time Checks](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/approval-criteria/alt-time-checks): altTimeChecks: deny transfers by hour, weekday, month, day of month, or ISO week, in UTC or with a timezone offset.
  - [Approval Trackers](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/approval-criteria/approval-trackers): approvalAmounts and maxNumTransfers: increment-only trackers that cap amounts and transfer counts, overall or per address, with periodic resets.
  - [Auto-Deletion](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/approval-criteria/auto-deletion): autoDeletionOptions: delete an approval after one use or after its transfer cap, and let counterparties or anyone purge it.
  - [Coin Transfers](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/approval-criteria/coin-transfers): coinTransfers: move x/bank coins (BADGE, IBC coins, alias denoms) every time an approval is used, plus the mint escrow address that pays on behalf of Mint.
  - [Dynamic Store Challenges](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/approval-criteria/dynamic-store-challenges): dynamicStoreChallenges: require the initiator, sender, recipient, or a fixed address to be true in an address-to-bool store with a global kill switch.
  - [ETH Signature Challenges](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/approval-criteria/eth-signature-challenges): ethSignatureChallenges: require a one-time Ethereum signature from a named signer over a message bound to the transfer context.
  - [EVM Query Challenges](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/approval-criteria/evm-query-challenges): evmQueryChallenges: gate an approval on a read-only EVM query whose result must compare as expected, with placeholders for the transfer parties.
  - [Invariants](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/approval-criteria/invariants): Creation-only collection rules: ownership times, supply caps, backed paths, forceful transfers, pool creation, and post-transfer EVM checks.
  - [Merkle Challenges](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/approval-criteria/merkle-challenges): merkleChallenges: gate an approval on a SHA256 Merkle proof for whitelists or claim codes, with per-leaf use limits and leaf signatures against front-running.
  - [Overrides](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/approval-criteria/overrides): overridesFromOutgoingApprovals and overridesToIncomingApprovals: bypass user-level approvals, the Mint requirement, and reserved-address protection.
  - [Predetermined Balances](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/approval-criteria/predetermined-balances): predeterminedBalances: force each use of an approval to move exact balances in order, by manual list or increments, with precalculation and scaling.
  - [Special Address Flags](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/approval-criteria/special-address-flags): allowBackedMinting and allowSpecialWrapping: opt a collection approval into backed-path and wrapper-path transfers, and the rules enforced.
  - [Token Ownership](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/approval-criteria/token-ownership): mustOwnTokens: require the initiator, sender, recipient, or a fixed address to hold tokens from some collection before the transfer is approved.
  - [User Approval Settings](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/approval-criteria/user-approval-settings): userApprovalSettings: let a collection approval restrict the denoms in user-level coin transfers, disable them, and take a royalty on every coin payment.
  - [Voting Challenges](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/approval-criteria/voting-challenges): votingChallenges: require a weighted quorum of on-chain votes from named voters, with partial votes, reset after execution, and a timelock.
- [Messages](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages): Every x/tokenization message, who signs it, and what it does. One page per message.
  - [MsgCreateCollection](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-create-collection): MsgCreateCollection creates a new collection. The only message that can set defaultBalances and invariants.
  - [MsgUpdateCollection](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-update-collection): MsgUpdateCollection updates an existing collection's fields with update flags. Manager only, permissions enforced.
  - [MsgUniversalUpdateCollection](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-universal-update-collection): MsgUniversalUpdateCollection creates or updates a collection in one legacy interface. All other collection messages route through it.
  - [MsgDeleteCollection](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-delete-collection): MsgDeleteCollection deletes a collection and purges its balances and trackers. Manager only, needs canDeleteCollection.
  - [MsgTransferTokens](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-transfer-tokens): MsgTransferTokens moves tokens between addresses. Each transfer must pass collection, outgoing, and incoming approvals.
  - [MsgUpdateUserApprovals](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-update-user-approvals): MsgUpdateUserApprovals replaces a user's outgoing and incoming approvals, auto-approve flags, and user permissions in one collection.
  - [MsgSetIncomingApproval](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-set-incoming-approval): MsgSetIncomingApproval creates or replaces one incoming approval by ID without rebuilding the full approval list.
  - [MsgDeleteIncomingApproval](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-delete-incoming-approval): MsgDeleteIncomingApproval deletes one incoming approval by ID without rebuilding the full approval list.
  - [MsgSetOutgoingApproval](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-set-outgoing-approval): MsgSetOutgoingApproval creates or replaces one outgoing approval by ID without rebuilding the full approval list.
  - [MsgDeleteOutgoingApproval](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-delete-outgoing-approval): MsgDeleteOutgoingApproval deletes one outgoing approval by ID without rebuilding the full approval list.
  - [MsgPurgeApprovals](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-purge-approvals): MsgPurgeApprovals removes expired user approvals, your own or another user's when their auto-deletion options allow it.
  - [MsgSetCollectionApprovals](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-set-collection-approvals): MsgSetCollectionApprovals replaces a collection's approvals and sets the canUpdateCollectionApprovals permission in one message.
  - [MsgSetValidTokenIds](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-set-valid-token-ids): MsgSetValidTokenIds sets a collection's validTokenIds and the canUpdateValidTokenIds permission in one message.
  - [MsgSetManager](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-set-manager): MsgSetManager transfers a collection's manager role and sets the canUpdateManager permission in one message.
  - [MsgSetCollectionMetadata](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-set-collection-metadata): MsgSetCollectionMetadata sets a collection's metadata URI or inline customData and the canUpdateCollectionMetadata permission.
  - [MsgSetTokenMetadata](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-set-token-metadata): MsgSetTokenMetadata sets per-token metadata entries and the canUpdateTokenMetadata permission in one message.
  - [MsgSetCustomData](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-set-custom-data): MsgSetCustomData sets a collection's customData string and the canUpdateCustomData permission in one message.
  - [MsgSetStandards](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-set-standards): MsgSetStandards sets a collection's standards list and the canUpdateStandards permission in one message.
  - [MsgSetIsArchived](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-set-is-archived): MsgSetIsArchived archives or unarchives a collection and sets the canArchiveCollection permission in one message.
  - [MsgCreateAddressLists](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-create-address-lists): MsgCreateAddressLists creates immutable, reusable address lists that approvals and permissions reference by ID.
  - [MsgCreateDynamicStore](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-create-dynamic-store): MsgCreateDynamicStore creates an on-chain boolean store keyed by address, for use in dynamic store challenges.
  - [MsgUpdateDynamicStore](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-update-dynamic-store): MsgUpdateDynamicStore replaces a dynamic store's default value, global kill switch, and metadata. Creator only.
  - [MsgDeleteDynamicStore](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-delete-dynamic-store): MsgDeleteDynamicStore deletes a dynamic store. Creator only.
  - [MsgSetDynamicStoreValue](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-set-dynamic-store-value): MsgSetDynamicStoreValue sets the boolean for one address in a dynamic store. Creator only.
  - [MsgCastVote](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-cast-vote): MsgCastVote casts or updates a weighted yes/no vote on a voting challenge inside an approval's criteria.
  - [MsgSetReservedProtocolAddress](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-set-reserved-protocol-address): MsgSetReservedProtocolAddress marks or unmarks an address as a reserved protocol address. Governance only.
  - [MsgUpdateParams](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/messages/msg-update-params): MsgUpdateParams replaces the x/tokenization module parameters (allowed denoms and affiliate percentage). Governance only.
- [Queries](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/queries): Every x/tokenization gRPC query with its LCD REST path and bb CLI command. One page per query.
  - [GetCollection](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/queries/get-collection): GetCollection returns the full on-chain record of a collection by ID.
  - [GetCollectionStats](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/queries/get-collection-stats): GetCollectionStats returns a collection's unique holder count and circulating supply.
  - [GetBalance](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/queries/get-balance): GetBalance returns an address's balances, approvals, auto-approve flags, and permissions in a collection.
  - [GetBalanceForToken](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/queries/get-balance-for-token): GetBalanceForToken returns the amount of one token ID an address owns at one point in time.
  - [GetWrappableBalances](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/queries/get-wrappable-balances): GetWrappableBalances returns the maximum amount of a wrapper or alias denom an address can mint from its token balances.
  - [GetAddressList](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/queries/get-address-list): GetAddressList returns an address list by ID, including reserved IDs such as All, Mint, and inverted lists.
  - [GetApprovalTracker](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/queries/get-approval-tracker): GetApprovalTracker returns the cumulative transfer count and amounts recorded for an approval's tracker.
  - [GetChallengeTracker](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/queries/get-challenge-tracker): GetChallengeTracker returns how many times a Merkle leaf has been used for a Merkle challenge.
  - [GetETHSignatureTracker](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/queries/get-eth-signature-tracker): GetETHSignatureTracker returns how many times an Ethereum signature has been used for an ETH signature challenge.
  - [GetDynamicStore](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/queries/get-dynamic-store): GetDynamicStore returns a dynamic store's creator, default value, global kill switch, and metadata.
  - [GetDynamicStoreValue](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/queries/get-dynamic-store-value): GetDynamicStoreValue returns the boolean stored for one address in a dynamic store.
  - [GetVote](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/queries/get-vote): GetVote returns one voter's current vote on a voting challenge.
  - [GetVotes](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/queries/get-votes): GetVotes returns every stored vote on a voting challenge proposal.
  - [IsAddressReservedProtocol](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/queries/is-address-reserved-protocol): IsAddressReservedProtocol returns whether an address is a reserved protocol address.
  - [GetAllReservedProtocolAddresses](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/queries/get-all-reserved-protocol-addresses): GetAllReservedProtocolAddresses returns every address flagged as a reserved protocol address.
  - [Params](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/queries/params): Params returns the x/tokenization module parameters (allowed denoms and affiliate percentage).
- [IBC and Wrapping](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/ibc): How x/tokenization tokens reach x/bank, IBC, and other chains. Map of the four mechanisms and when to use each.
  - [Alias Denoms](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/ibc/alias-denoms): The badgeslp:COLLECTION_ID:denom alias format that lets Cosmos SDK interfaces treat x/tokenization balances as sdk.Coin without wrapping.
  - [Cosmos Coin Wrapper Paths](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/ibc/cosmos-coin-wrapper-paths): Wrapper paths burn native tokens into a generated badges:COLLECTION_ID:denom x/bank coin and back. Fields, conversion rates, {id} denoms, approvals.
  - [Backed Minting](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/ibc/backed-minting): Backed paths back every token 1:1 with an existing IBC coin through a protocol-controlled special address. Invariant setup, conversion, Mint rules, approvals.
  - [Transfer Tokens Hook](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/ibc/transfer-tokens-hook): The x/custom-hooks IBC middleware: transfer_tokens (run MsgTransferTokens on an inbound transfer) and swap_and_action (swap, then transfer or forward).
- [Integrate the Module](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/integrate): For Cosmos SDK chain developers who embed x/tokenization in their own app. What the module needs from app.go and where each integration pattern lives.
  - [Multiple Standards](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/integrate/multiple-standards): A send manager with alias denom routing lets one BankKeeper-shaped call move x/bank coins and native tokens. Prefix matching, auto-scan, routing.
  - [Extension Hooks](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/integrate/extension-hooks): Three app.go registration points for chain-wide invariants: approval criteria checkers, global transfer checkers, and collection verifiers.
  - [Ante Handler Token Gates](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/integrate/ante-handler-token-gates): Gate any Cosmos SDK message type on token ownership with one ante decorator: circuit breakers, KYC sends, compliant staking, governance gates.
  - [Proof-of-Token Voting Power](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/integrate/proof-of-token-voting-power): A design proposal for gating validator voting power on a credential token. No x/pot module ships; this is app-level design guidance for chain teams.
- [BB-402](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/bb-402): Gate any HTTP API behind on-chain token ownership with the 402 status code. Flow, 402 body, X-BB-Proof header, AccessCondition, response codes.
  - [Specification](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/bb-402/spec): BB-402 protocol specification v1 (draft, 2026-03-05): flow, message formats, AccessCondition grammar, verification, security, versioning, x402 comparison.
  - [Collection Recipes](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard/bb-402/collection-recipes): Collection approval configurations for BB-402 auth patterns: basic soulbound access token, revocable token, short-lived 2FA token, ban list, and tiered access.
- [Source Code](https://github.com/BitBadges/bitbadgeschain/tree/master/x/tokenization)

## Chain

- [Overview](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain): The BitBadges chain: what runs on it, chain IDs, the BADGE denom and EVM decimals, public endpoints (RPC, LCD, EVM RPC, explorer, chain registry), IBC channels.
- [Chain API Reference](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain-api-reference)
- [Modules](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/modules): Every BitBadges-specific Cosmos SDK module: x/tokenization (the token standard), gamm, poolmanager, sendmanager, managersplitter, and the IBC middleware.
  - [x/tokenization](https://docs.bitbadges.io/token-standard): What the x/tokenization module is, how its pieces fit together, and the order to read this tab in.
  - [x/gamm](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/modules/gamm): The x/gamm AMM module, forked from Osmosis. How pools hold native tokens through badgeslp alias denoms and why pool trades still obey collection approvals.
    - [Messages](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/modules/gamm/messages): All 12 x/gamm messages with fields and a JSON example each: pool creation, join, exit, swaps, single-asset joins and exits, stableswap, IBC swap.
    - [Queries](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/modules/gamm/queries): All 16 x/gamm queries with LCD paths and live mainnet examples: pools, liquidity, shares, spot price, join and exit calculators, estimates, params.
  - [x/managersplitter](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/modules/manager-splitter): x/managersplitter: a module-derived proxy address that acts as collection manager while each permission is delegated to approved addresses.
    - [Messages and Queries](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/modules/manager-splitter/messages): x/managersplitter messages (create, update, delete, execute, update params) and the three queries, with fields, permission checks, and JSON examples.
  - [x/sendmanager](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/modules/send-manager): x/sendmanager routes sdk.Coins by denom prefix to x/bank or x/tokenization. MsgSendWithAliasRouting, balance query, keeper API, send precompile.
  - [x/poolmanager](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/modules/pool-manager): x/poolmanager: pool ID registry, cross-pool swap routing, split routes, taker fees, and the estimate endpoints that replace the deprecated gamm ones.
  - [x/ibc-rate-limit](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/modules/ibc-rate-limit): The x/ibc-rate-limit middleware: per channel and denom caps on supply shift, unique senders, and per-address transfers, plus the governance messages.
- [Proto reference](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/proto): Generated reference for every protobuf message and service in the chain modules. Browse on the site.
- [EVM](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/evm): How the BitBadges EVM works: three custom precompiles that expose the tokenization, gamm, and send manager modules to Solidity contracts.
  - [Solidity Quickstart](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/evm/solidity-quickstart): Get from zero to a working Solidity contract on BitBadges precompiles in five minutes: constants, addresses, JSON helpers, common patterns, errors.
  - [Setup](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/evm/setup): Chain IDs, RPC ports, starting a local node with JSON-RPC, MetaMask config, a minimal contract, deploy script, frontend hook, and troubleshooting.
  - [Developer Guide](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/evm/developer-guide): Rules for the BitBadges EVM: which keys sign which transactions, address conversion, msg.sender inside a precompile, and 9 vs 18 decimals.
  - [Architecture](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/evm/architecture): The call path from a Solidity contract through a Go precompile to a Cosmos SDK keeper, the package layout, and how to add methods or precompiles.
  - [Tokenization Precompile](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/evm/tokenization-precompile): The tokenization precompile at 0x...1001: the token standard from Solidity through JSON messages, with helpers, patterns, and executeMultiple.
    - [API](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/evm/tokenization-precompile/api): Every function on the tokenization precompile from abi.json: 25 transactions, executeMultiple, 17 queries, 7 utilities, with signatures and JSON.
    - [Gas](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/evm/tokenization-precompile/gas): Tokenization precompile gas: per-method base costs, the fixed buffers RequiredGas adds, executeMultiple and input-size costs, per-element constants.
    - [Errors](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/evm/tokenization-precompile/errors): Tokenization precompile errors: the nine codes from errors.go, the uint64 range trap, common failures with fixes, Solidity handling, debugging.
    - [Security](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/evm/tokenization-precompile/security): The tokenization precompile security model from security.go: caller checks, overflow, validation, DoS limits, error sanitization, threat model.
  - [Gamm Precompile](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/evm/gamm-precompile): The GAMM precompile at 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001002: join and exit pools, swap, swap with an IBC transfer, create and query pools from Solidity.
    - [API](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/evm/gamm-precompile/api): GAMM precompile reference: the 14-function Solidity interface, the snake_case JSON for each message and query, gas constants, and error codes.
    - [Gotchas](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/evm/gamm-precompile/gotchas): Mistakes that break GAMM precompile calls: string pool IDs, integer amounts, snake_case keys, tuple and bytes returns, slippage, multi-hop routes.
  - [Send Manager Precompile](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/evm/send-manager-precompile): The send manager precompile at 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001003: one send method that moves native coins and alias denoms from a contract via x/bank.
  - [Cosmos Precompiles](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/evm/cosmos-precompiles): The upstream cosmos/evm precompiles on BitBadges (P256, bech32, staking, distribution, IBC, bank, governance, slashing, ICS02) with addresses and methods.
  - [RPC Endpoints](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/evm/rpc-endpoints): Public EVM JSON-RPC endpoints for BitBadges, supported methods, ethers.js, Hardhat and Foundry config, and running your own JSON-RPC node.
- [Cross-Chain Queries](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/cross-chain-queries): Interchain queries let another Cosmos chain verify x/tokenization ownership over IBC without moving tokens. Packet types, channel setup, Go examples.
- [Supported Denoms](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/supported-denoms): The x/tokenization allowed_denoms list on mainnet, the SDK coin registry, and the canonical USDC (via Injective) versus legacy USDC.n (via Noble) policy.
- [Run a Node](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/run-a-node): Start a BitBadges mainnet full node or validator: init, genesis, peers, timeout_commit, EVM chain ID, sync check, snapshots, Cosmovisor, JSON-RPC settings.
- [Testnet](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/testnet): Testnet status (offline since 2026-04-25), how to test on mainnet as a chaosnet instead, and the testnet endpoints and faucet API kept for when it returns.
- [WebSocket Events](https://docs.bitbadges.io/chain/websocket-events): Subscribe to chain events over the CometBFT WebSocket: endpoint, subscribe and unsubscribe, queries by message type and sender, a Node.js listener.
- [Source Code](https://github.com/BitBadges/bitbadgeschain)
- [Chain Registry](https://github.com/cosmos/chain-registry/tree/master/bitbadges)

## API

- [Overview](https://docs.bitbadges.io/api): The BitBadges API in one page. Base URL, API keys, credits and pricing, rate limits, number types, errors, and the refresh queue.
- [API Reference](https://docs.bitbadges.io/api-reference)
- [Pagination and Views](https://docs.bitbadges.io/api/pagination-and-views): Bookmark pagination and the views object in BitBadges API responses, with the SDK helpers that page through them.
- [Swaps](https://docs.bitbadges.io/api/swaps): Estimate a token swap through the BitBadges API. Payload, response, Skip Go compatibility, and how to execute the returned messages.
- [Claims](https://docs.bitbadges.io/api/claims): How claims work. Plugins, indexed versus on-demand, claim numbers, success logic, sign-in modes, gating an on-chain approval, and the trust model.
  - [Endpoints](https://docs.bitbadges.io/api/claims/endpoints): Claims API reference. Complete, simulate, and verify claims, fetch and search them, create and delete them, and build the merkle proof for on-chain claims.
  - [Plugins](https://docs.bitbadges.io/api/claims/plugins): Every claim plugin id with its parameters, state, and where it runs, plus the request and response contract for custom plugin endpoints.
  - [Dynamic Stores](https://docs.bitbadges.io/api/claims/dynamic-stores): Dynamic stores are BitBadges-hosted address lists you update by API, UI, or Zapier and attach to claims through the whitelist plugin.
- [Sign In with BitBadges](https://docs.bitbadges.io/api/sign-in): Sign In with BitBadges (SIWBB) is an OAuth 2.0 flow that proves address ownership and grants your app BitBadges API scopes.
  - [Setup](https://docs.bitbadges.io/api/sign-in/setup): Register an OAuth app in the BitBadges developer portal and get the client ID, client secret, and redirect URIs that Sign In with BitBadges needs.
  - [Authorization URL](https://docs.bitbadges.io/api/sign-in/authorization-url): Build the Sign In with BitBadges authorization URL. Parameters, scopes, attaching a claim, and the SDK helper that generates it.
  - [Callback](https://docs.bitbadges.io/api/sign-in/callback): Handle the Sign In with BitBadges redirect callback. Read code and state from the query string, then exchange the code.
  - [Verification](https://docs.bitbadges.io/api/sign-in/verification): Exchange a Sign In with BitBadges code for the address and tokens, manage access and refresh tokens, and know what is verified natively and what is not.
  - [Frameworks](https://docs.bitbadges.io/api/sign-in/frameworks): Use Sign In with BitBadges through Auth0, WordPress, Supabase, Discourse, Passport.js, and other frameworks that already speak OAuth 2.0.

## SDK & CLI

- [SDK](https://docs.bitbadges.io/sdk): Install the bitbadges TypeScript SDK, create a BitBadgesAPI client, sign and broadcast transactions, and find the helper you need.
  - [React Quickstart](https://docs.bitbadges.io/sdk/react-quickstart): Wire BitBadges into a React or Next.js app: install, connect a wallet, query a collection, and sign and broadcast.
  - [Types](https://docs.bitbadges.io/sdk/types): How SDK types are exported (classes, interfaces, typed arrays, proto), the NumberType generic, and the BigIntify, Numberify, and Stringify converters.
  - [Snippets](https://docs.bitbadges.io/sdk/snippets): Verified TypeScript examples for the bitbadges SDK helpers, balances, uint ranges, transfers, address lists, metadata, approvals, and interpreters.
    - [Address Conversions](https://docs.bitbadges.io/sdk/snippets/address-conversions): Convert between 0x Ethereum addresses and bb1 BitBadges addresses, and validate addresses, with the bitbadges SDK.
    - [Uint Ranges](https://docs.bitbadges.io/sdk/snippets/uint-ranges): UintRange and UintRangeArray helpers in the bitbadges SDK, sort and merge, search, invert, remove, and overlap checks.
    - [Balances](https://docs.bitbadges.io/sdk/snippets/balances): Create, add, subtract, and look up balances with BalanceArray and the balance helper functions in the bitbadges SDK.
    - [Balance Lookups](https://docs.bitbadges.io/sdk/snippets/balance-lookups): Fetch a user's balance for a collection or a single token from the BitBadges API, the chain, or the bb CLI, full balance array or one amount.
    - [Transfers](https://docs.bitbadges.io/sdk/snippets/transfers): Use TransferWithIncrements in the bitbadges SDK to describe batch transfers with incrementing token IDs or ownership times, and compute the resulting balances.
    - [Address Lists](https://docs.bitbadges.io/sdk/snippets/address-lists): Build and query AddressList objects in the bitbadges SDK, membership checks, inversion, removal, and the reserved Mint and All lists.
    - [Token Metadata](https://docs.bitbadges.io/sdk/snippets/token-metadata): Read, update, and remove per-token metadata with the TokenMetadataDetails helpers in the bitbadges SDK.
    - [Approvals](https://docs.bitbadges.io/sdk/snippets/approvals): Find the unhandled (disapproved) transfer combinations in a set of approvals and append the default self-initiated user approvals with the bitbadges SDK.
    - [Interpret a Collection](https://docs.bitbadges.io/sdk/snippets/interpret-collection): Generate a plain-language markdown report of any on-chain collection with interpretCollection in the bitbadges SDK.
    - [Interpret a Transaction](https://docs.bitbadges.io/sdk/snippets/interpret-transaction): Explain an unsigned MsgUniversalUpdateCollection transaction body in plain language with interpretTransaction in the bitbadges SDK.
    - [Simulation Balance Diffs](https://docs.bitbadges.io/sdk/snippets/simulation-balance-diffs): Turn chain simulation events into per-address coin and token balance changes with simulateAndReview, parseSimulationEvents, and calculateNetChanges.
  - [Transactions](https://docs.bitbadges.io/sdk/transactions): The TypeScript transaction pipeline: build messages, create a transaction context, produce the payload, sign with a Cosmos or EVM wallet, and broadcast.
    - [Signing Client](https://docs.bitbadges.io/sdk/transactions/signing-client): BitBadgesSigningClient reference, wallet adapters for Keplr, Leap, MetaMask, mnemonics and private keys, network presets, gas, sequence retry, and results.
    - [Sign with Cosmos Wallets](https://docs.bitbadges.io/sdk/transactions/sign-cosmos): Sign a BitBadges transaction payload by hand with Keplr or another Cosmos wallet using signDirect, then build the broadcast body.
    - [Sign with Ethereum Wallets](https://docs.bitbadges.io/sdk/transactions/sign-ethereum): Sign a BitBadges transaction by hand with MetaMask, Privy, or ethers.js by sending the payload's EVM precompile call.
    - [Broadcast](https://docs.bitbadges.io/sdk/transactions/broadcast): Simulate a signed BitBadges transaction, broadcast it through the API or a node, and poll for the receipt; plus the bitbadges.io developer broadcast page.
- [SDK Reference](https://docs.bitbadges.io/sdk/reference): Generated TypeDoc for every exported class, function and type. Browse on the site; the full corpus dump excludes it too.
- [CLI](https://docs.bitbadges.io/cli): Install the bb CLI, learn its command groups, configure settings and API keys, and run doctor and completion.
  - [build](https://docs.bitbadges.io/cli/build): Reference for every bb build subcommand, the shared flags, metadata modes, JSON input, and the walkthrough transfer builder.
  - [check, explain, simulate, preview](https://docs.bitbadges.io/cli/analyze): Inspect a built transaction before signing with bb check, bb explain, bb simulate, and bb preview.
  - [deploy and tx](https://docs.bitbadges.io/cli/deploy): Sign and broadcast with bb deploy (browser wallet, keyring, burner, or generated payload), confirm with bb tx status and tx wait, and use the sign bridge.
  - [standards](https://docs.bitbadges.io/cli/standards): End-user verbs for every BitBadges standard: list, show, status, and the action that emits a ready-to-sign message.
  - [api](https://docs.bitbadges.io/cli/api): Call any BitBadges API route from the terminal with bb api, search routes, print schemas, and attach a session.
  - [auth](https://docs.bitbadges.io/cli/auth): Create and manage BitBadges API user sessions from the CLI with bb auth, using a browser wallet or any external signer.
  - [account and url](https://docs.bitbadges.io/cli/account): Read an address profile, tokens, balances, activity, and approvals; convert and validate addresses; derive alias addresses and public keys; resolve URLs.
  - [swap, pools, and amounts](https://docs.bitbadges.io/cli/swap): DEX and swap commands: estimate and execute swaps, browse pools and asset pairs, read prices and balances, and do coin amount math.
  - [dev](https://docs.bitbadges.io/cli/dev): The agent-facing bb dev surface: call MCP builder tools directly, read resources, browse docs and skills, and send feedback.
  - [Chain Commands](https://docs.bitbadges.io/cli/chain): Chain-native bb commands from bitbadgeschaind: keys, tx, query, sign-arbitrary, genesis, and node operation.

## Agents

- [AI Agents](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents): Install paths, quickstart, and the review-and-sign handoff for AI agents and bots that build on BitBadges.
- [Set Up Your AI](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/setup): Set up your AI harness for BitBadges: the MCP server command and the config for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Codex CLI, VS Code, and Zed.
- [MCP Builder Tools](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/mcp-tools): Reference for the MCP builder tools. Install, client configs, every tool with its key params, workflows, resources, and the CLI access path.
- [Claude Code Plugin](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/claude-code-plugin): Install and use the BitBadges Claude Code plugin. It wires the MCP builder tools and adds 8 workflow skills, two slash commands, and a builder subagent.
- [Programmatic Agent](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/programmatic-agent): Build collections from natural-language prompts in Node with BitBadgesBuilderAgent and your own Anthropic or OpenAI key: config, hooks, sessions, handoff.
- [Spending Authorization](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/spending-authorization): Give an AI agent a delegate wallet with chain-enforced spending limits: daily caps, time windows, recipient and token allowlists, one-transaction revocation.
- [Bot Examples](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/bot-examples): Copy-paste bot patterns on mainnet. Mint a fungible token, conditional transfer, ownership gating, event subscription, and the builder tool workflow.
- [Reading the Docs (llms.txt)](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/reading-the-docs): How an agent reads these docs. llms.txt, the full-text dump, bb dev docs, the fetch_docs MCP tool, and the URL patterns of this site.
- [Skills](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/skills): The builder skills: the instruction text AI agents load to build a specific token type or feature on BitBadges.
  - [Smart Token](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/skills/smart-token): IBC-backed smart token with 1:1 backing and two required approvals (backing + unbacking)
  - [Minting](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/skills/minting): Mint approval patterns including public mint, whitelist mint, creator-only mint, payment-gated mint, and escrow payouts
  - [Liquidity Pools](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/skills/liquidity-pools): Liquidity pool standard with the "Liquidity Pools" protocol standard tag, used for tradable assets that can be swapped on a DEX
  - [Fungible Token](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/skills/fungible-token): Simple fungible token with fixed or unlimited supply and configurable mint/transfer approvals
  - [NFT Collection](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/skills/nft-collection): Non-fungible token collection with unique token IDs, metadata URIs, and badge-based ownership
  - [Subscription](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/skills/subscription): Time-based subscription token with recurring payment approvals and auto-deletion on expiry
  - [Transferability and Update Rules](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/skills/immutability): Lock collection permissions to make properties permanently immutable or permanently permitted
  - [Custom 2FA](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/skills/custom-2fa): Two-factor authentication for transfers using a secondary approval address
  - [Address List](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/skills/address-list): On-chain address list where membership = owning x1 of token ID 1. Manager can add/remove addresses.
  - [BB-402 Token-Gated Access](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/skills/bb-402): Token-gated access protocol where ownership of specific badges grants API/resource access
  - [Burnable](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/skills/burnable): Allow token holders to burn tokens by sending them to the burn address, permanently removing them from circulation
  - [Multi-Sig and Voting](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/skills/multi-sig-voting): Require weighted quorum voting from multiple parties before transfers can proceed (multi-sig, governance, etc.)
  - [Payment Protocol](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/skills/payment-protocol): Invoices, escrows, bounties, milestones, and multi-party agreements using coinTransfer-based approvals or IBC-backed smart token escrow
  - [Tradable NFTs](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/skills/tradable): NFT marketplace standard enabling peer-to-peer transfers with the "NFTMarketplace" standard tag and NFTPricingDenom
  - [Credit Token](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/skills/credit-token): Increment-only, non-transferable credit token purchased with any ICS20 denom. Users pay X of a denom and receive Y tokens as credits/proof of payment. For a 1:1 backed token with on-chain transferability, use the Smart Token standard instead.
  - [Auto-Mint](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/skills/auto-mint): Mint and distribute tokens to recipients at collection creation time using MsgTransferTokens
  - [Quest](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/skills/quest): Quest/reward collection: users complete criteria and claim a badge + coin payout
  - [Prediction Market](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/skills/prediction-market): Binary prediction market with YES/NO outcome tokens, liquidity pool trading, and vote-based settlement
  - [Bounty](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/skills/bounty): Escrow-based bounty with verifier arbitration. Submitter escrows coins, verifier accepts (pays recipient) or denies (refunds submitter). Expires if no decision.
  - [Payment Request](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/skills/payment-request): Agent-initiated payment request with no escrow. The agent (or any address) creates a collection requesting payment from a targeted human payer. The payer approves and pays from their own wallet in a single action. Inverse of Bounty.
  - [Crowdfund](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/skills/crowdfund): On-chain crowdfunding with goal tracking via mustOwnTokens. Contributors deposit funds, receive refund tokens. Crowdfunder withdraws if goal met, contributors refund if not.
  - [Auction](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/skills/auction): Single-item auction with intent-based bidding. Seller mints NFT directly to the winning bidder during the accept window.
  - [Products](https://docs.bitbadges.io/agents/skills/product-catalog): Multi-product storefront with per-product pricing, supply limits, and optional burn-on-purchase. Each product is a separate token ID.
